evidence: 0093 (owner decisions of 2026-10-28, patient parity with hid-1.0; migrations pre-approved for this batch) is additive. Identity's runtime reads identity.patients only through RLS, which lets system:auth see public-enrollment patients alone (0051), so every lookup that must also find a patient migrated from hid-1.0 is a SECURITY DEFINER function with search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp. New functions: auth.find_patient_account(kind, value) (system:auth; by Health ID, phone contact-lookup HMAC (or a Nigerian number's two, its +234 and +2340 forms comma separated, because hid-1.0 stored a trunk 0 typed after +234 and the importer kept it; one account across both or nothing), compared as char(64) so that patients_phone_hmac_uq answers it, or account id; the one active patient's account, any status but deleted, with the workforce flag, the verified-email flag and the patient's first name and Health ID; nothing when none or several accounts match; the password hash only for Health ID and phone) for patient sign-in, recovery start and the reset emails; auth.patient_email_registered(email, HMAC) (system:auth; Google sign-up answers GOOGLE_ACCOUNT_EXISTS); auth.link_google_identity_by_verified_email(subject, email, HMAC) (system:auth; a linked subject answers suspended for a suspended patient, else already_linked; otherwise under an advisory lock on the email, the candidates from two index lookups (accounts_email_ci_uq, patients_email_hmac_uq) unioned: none, ambiguous, workforce, not_verified, suspended, linked_elsewhere, or the link with source_system hid-google-verified-email-link, an auth.google.auto-link audit row and the SECURITY_GOOGLE_LINKED inbox notice; account then patient locked FOR UPDATE as 0059; unique (issuer, subject) settles a race as already_linked); auth.record_account_security_notice(account, code) (system:auth; SECURITY_PASSWORD_RESET_REQUESTED, SECURITY_PASSWORD_CHANGED, SECURITY_GOOGLE_LINKED, resource type account, no resource id, empty metadata, for the account's active patient only, only with evidence of the last 10 minutes, once per evidence, a reset request at most hourly; null otherwise, never raising); identity.count_my_unread_notifications(subject, session) (live patient session; unread inbox plus unread imported hid-1.0 items, each counted to 1000, at most 1000); identity.patient_self_access_log(subject, session, limit, before) (live patient session; newest first, the patient's own successful application audit events of record views and changes (document downloads and OCR source reads, OCR reads, routed orders sent and withdrawn, read, accepted, marked cannot complete or wrong patient, or corrected by the receiving laboratory or pharmacy, and work items accepted among them), access grants and ends and emergency access, read through audit_patient_time_idx, at most 2000 rows a call, consecutive views or changes by one person at one facility under 10 minutes apart as one entry; each entry id, at, action, actorKind, actorName (clinician), facilityName; never a record, resource id, reason, address or user agent; keyset next). Replaced bodies, each pinned by md5 of pg_proc.prosrc before (0092's bd9190beca14e04b46eb3399910dcd73, 0010's 16b9fd3d2fe5d6f803d532e1dd0f91a7) and after (b21ffc9d2426c988b0b358e5718542ed, d13df3197640316324948268d7d9a18f): identity.activate_public_patient_signup, 0092's body byte for byte but the profile phone rule ^\+234[0-9]{10}$ becoming ^\+[1-9][0-9]{6,14}$ (E.164 of any country); identity.close_own_consent_grant, 0010's body plus the CONSENT_GRANT_ENDED_BY_CLINICIAN inbox notice (resource consent-grant, the grant id, metadata facilityName only, never the reason) when an active grant is closed before it expires, never on a replay; their answers, audit rows, refusals, owners, ACLs, language, volatility and search_path unchanged (post-checked in the migration). Preconditions (55000, nothing applied): prerequisites exist; no object of 0093 exists under any signature (already applied); the two replaced bodies and 17 relied-on bodies pinned by md5; the inbox code, resource type and metadata CHECKs, audit_patient_time_idx and the patients' Health ID and phone unique indexes pinned by definition; the applying role holds, by ownership, membership or grant and never a superuser's bypass, ownership of identity.patients and every privilege the new bodies need, owns the replaced functions, and the close's owner may run the inbox writer and read identity.facilities (42501 otherwise). Locks: none on any application table and none on any existing function (no table, index, CHECK or trigger is created or altered; every body is PL/pgSQL; section 0 reads catalogs only). Measured with pg_locks before commit: ACCESS SHARE on the auth and identity schemas, the plpgsql language and the two runtime roles; SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE on five new functions (comments); ACCESS EXCLUSIVE only on the migration's own temporary table and helper and the session's temporary schema. Grants: the six new functions to hid_identity_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime (revoked from PUBLIC), in the migration and in runtime-grants.sql; the replaced functions keep their ACLs. Measured on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 cluster with the repository's runner: 0001-0092 applied and roles bootstrapped, then 0093 planned, dry-run and applied (33 ms), a rerun found 0 pending, the file applied again stopped with 55000 0093: already applied, the role bootstrap and verify-roles passed; a fresh database took 0001-0093 in one dry run and one apply; a copy whose schemas, tables and functions belong to a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner applied 0093 as that owner; a copy with a drifted replaced body (close) or relied-on body (the inbox writer) stopped with nothing applied, and so did an applying role that does not own identity.patients or the replaced function. All 16 database/tests and 49 test/database suites pass on the upgraded and the fresh copy, among them the new patient-parity-identity suite (security properties and grants; international, 7-digit and Nigerian sign-up phones activate, a number without + is refused, a replay unchanged; a migrated patient found by Health ID and phone where RLS hides it, by either of a Nigerian number's two HMACs, two accounts across them answering nothing, the phone through patients_phone_hmac_uq and the Google candidates through accounts_email_ci_uq and patients_email_hmac_uq with 2,000 analyzed other patients, suspended, workforce, deleted and malformed cases, system:auth only; every Google outcome with the link, audit and notice rows; security notices with evidence, dedupe and refusals, the explicit link's and a completed recovery's notices; the early-end notice once, none on replay, after expiry or for a deleted login, the close's answer and audit unchanged, another clinician P0002; the unread count bound to the live session; the access log's kinds, exclusions, names, collapsing, keyset pages, scan cap and session binding, document downloads, OCR reads and routed orders as views and changes; each fix reverted alone fails it), and seven definer suites pass with the NOSUPERUSER owner. A patient with 300,000 audit rows among 1,300,000 reads a 50- or 100-entry page in 70-110 ms, a page 200 days back in 35-60 ms (2,000-row index scan about 1 ms). On a copy with 50,000 patients a phone lookup takes 0.3 ms (an index scan of patients_phone_hmac_uq; a text comparison read every patient, 21 ms) and an unlinked Google sign-in's candidates 0.09 ms (index scans of accounts_email_ci_uq and patients_email_hmac_uq; one OR across both tables joined every patient, 36 ms). Old images on this schema: the previous Identity calls none of the new functions; its direct Health ID query still finds public-enrollment patients only, as before; its sign-up sends +234 numbers, which the replaced activation admits; a clinician's close answers as before with one more inbox row, which the previous website shows with its generic title. Applied migrations 0001-0092 are unchanged. 0094 (owner decisions of 2026-10-28, patient profile parity with hid-1.0, and the lead's decisions for wave B3; migrations pre-approved for this batch) is additive and is declared with 0093, which no release has applied yet. New tables, each under forced RLS: identity.patient_profile_details (the hospital the patient uses now and the HMO name, free text, each 1-120 characters, trimmed, without control characters, or null; row_version); identity.patient_profile_photos (Identity's AES-256-GCM ciphertext of a JPEG or PNG of at most 300 KB and 1-1024 pixels a side under identity:patient-photo:<patient>:<sha256>, its media type, sha256, size, dimensions and key version; the ciphertext is exactly the size plus 29 bytes); identity.patient_contact_changes (an email change pending with the new address encrypted under identity:patient-contact:<change>:email, its contact lookup HMAC, an HMAC of the 6-digit code bound to the change, expiry, attempts and delivery outcome, then completed; a phone change completed when made, the current password being its proof; a refused start kept invalidated without ciphertext so that it counts; one pending change per patient and channel; a ciphertext erased once superseded or invalidated; append-only, no delete); ehr.patient_reported_health_profiles (blood group A+ A- B+ B- AB+ AB- O+ O-, genotype AA AS AC SS SC CC, allergies, current medications, chronic conditions and medical notes, each 1-1000 characters with the newline the only control character, or null; who saved it; row_version). The three Identity tables have an owner policy only and no grant: only the new commands read or write them. The EHR table has the owner policy (its write command) and the read policy ehr.imported_record_read_context(patient_id), as 0062's imported profile: the patient in a fresh patient-self transaction (0083) or a clinician whose read_records access to the patient at the current facility is granted; SELECT to hid_ehr_runtime. 13 new SECURITY DEFINER functions with search_path pg_catalog, pg_temp: identity.patient_self_contact, my_contact_change_credentials, start_my_email_change (workforce for an account that is also a staff login by 0093's test (a platform role, a staff record or a facility membership), nothing recorded; unchanged, rate_limited at one start a resend window or five an hour, unavailable when another non-deleted account, another patient or a staff record (staff_email_ci_uq) holds the address, recorded and audited as denied; else the open change superseded and the pending one recorded), read_my_pending_email_change, record_my_contact_change_delivery (a definitive failure invalidates, audited as identity.patient.contact-change.delivery failure), complete_my_email_change (wrong codes counted, the fifth invalidates, expiry invalidates; the right one, under sign-up activation's advisory lock patient-contact:email:<HMAC>, the account then the patient locked FOR UPDATE as 0059, re-checks the address is free of other accounts, patients and staff records (unavailable) and that the account is not workforce (workforce, the change invalidated as workforce_account), sets auth.accounts.email and email_verified_at and identity.patients' email ciphertext and lookup HMAC, a unique violation answering unavailable; then revokes the account's active Google links with source_system hid-google-verified-email-link (0093's automatic link from the previous address; an explicit or sign-up link stays) with an auth.google.auto-link.revoke audit row, invalidates the account's open PASSWORD_RESET, LEGACY_ACCOUNT_RECOVERY and LEGACY_SESSION_FALLBACK codes ('completed', as 0029's completion) and revokes the account's sessions outside the caller's session family ('contact_changed', token_version unchanged so the caller's session goes on), the counts in the completion's audit details; and answers the previous address once for its notice), change_my_phone (unchanged in either Nigerian stored form unless Identity says it cannot read the stored number (a phone migrated from hid-1.0 under the migration's key), which is then written again under Identity's key as a completed change so that the profile shows it; rate_limited at five an hour, unavailable when another patient holds any form, recorded; else under the advisory lock patient-contact:phone:<HMAC> sets identity.patients' phone ciphertext and lookup HMAC, so phone sign-in and reset (0093's auth.find_patient_account) use the new number, and records the completed change; the notice address only when verified), read_my_profile_details, save_my_profile_details (conflict on a stale version), set_my_profile_photo, read_my_profile_photo and remove_my_profile_photo, each bound to identity.patient_self_session and a correlation id; and ehr.save_my_reported_health_profile, bound to ehr.patient_self_context(app.patient_id) (conflict on a stale version). Every write records its audit.events row in its transaction, without a contact, code, photo or health value; contact_key_version of identity.patients is set only where it was null. Replaced body, pinned by md5 of pg_proc.prosrc before (0057's d6838ccecab98c38059e66e04ad75cea) and after (e0370d523deb8fcfa40a33a41dfa9227): identity.patient_contact_lookup_ready, 0057's checks but that an active enrollment whose patient's contact on that channel was written by a completed contact change stays ready, and a contact a migrated patient added (none before) by a change completed after the rekey marker counts with the marker's contacts; the migrated patients' contacts are counted once before the marker is read; without contact changes the answer is 0057's; owner, ACL, language, volatility, SECURITY DEFINER and search_path unchanged (post-checked). Without it the first email change of a sign-up patient, or a phone change of a NIN-route patient, would make every sign-up and NIN start answer 503. scripts/rekey-patient-contact-lookups.mjs (not part of the release) skips a contact a completed change wrote instead of stopping on it. Preconditions (55000, nothing applied): prerequisites exist; no table or function of 0094 exists (already applied); the replaced body and 12 relied-on bodies (actor, correlation and facility readers, identity.patient_self_session, ehr.patient_self_context, ehr.imported_record_read_context, ehr.context_allows, identity.has_active_consent_grant, the audit trigger, platform.reject_mutation, identity.public_patient_contact_already_bound, auth.find_patient_account) pinned by md5; identity.patients' contact CHECKs, accounts_email_ci_uq, patients_email_hmac_uq, patients_phone_hmac_uq, staff_email_ci_uq, auth.otp_challenges' invalidation reasons and auth.external_identities' statuses pinned by definition; the applying role holds, by ownership, membership or grant and never a superuser's bypass, ownership of identity.patients and every privilege the new bodies need (among them UPDATE on auth.sessions, auth.otp_challenges and auth.external_identities and SELECT on auth.account_roles, identity.staff and identity.staff_facility_memberships), and is itself the readiness function's owner (42501 otherwise). Locks: SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE on auth.accounts and identity.patients (the new foreign keys), taken up front in that order, NOWAIT every 10 ms for at most 5 s (then 55P03, nothing applied), held to commit: they block writes to those tables, never reads. Measured with pg_locks before commit: SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE and ACCESS SHARE on auth.accounts and identity.patients, ACCESS SHARE on their primary keys; ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the four new tables, their indexes and TOAST tables; ACCESS SHARE on ehr.imported_record_read_context and platform.reject_mutation; SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE on five new functions (comments); ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the migration's own temporary table and helper and the session's temporary schema; no lock on any other application table (none on auth.sessions, auth.otp_challenges, auth.external_identities or the workforce tables). With a write held open on identity.patients the runner stopped after 5.3 s with 55P03 and nothing applied, then applied once it ended. Grants: the 12 Identity commands to hid_identity_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime, the EHR command and SELECT on the EHR table to hid_ehr_runtime and hid_schema_test_runtime, every new function revoked from PUBLIC, in the migration and in runtime-grants.sql; the replaced function keeps its ACL. Measured on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16 cluster with the repository's runner: 0001-0093 applied and roles bootstrapped, then 0094 planned, dry-run and applied (51 ms; 26 function and 2 table grants from the migration itself), a rerun found 0 pending, the file applied again stopped with 55000 0094: already applied, the role bootstrap and verify-roles passed; a fresh database took 0001-0094 in one dry run and one apply; a copy whose schemas, tables and functions belong to a NOSUPERUSER NOBYPASSRLS owner applied 0094 as that owner; copies with a drifted replaced body (the readiness function), a drifted relied-on body (identity.patient_self_session), a dropped contact CHECK, a changed recovery-code invalidation CHECK or a non-unique staff email index stopped with nothing applied, and so did an applying role that does not own identity.patients or the readiness function, or lacks UPDATE on auth.sessions and auth.external_identities. All 16 database/tests and 50 test/database suites pass on the upgraded and the fresh copy, among them the new patient-parity-profile suite (run as hid_identity_api_runtime and hid_ehr_api_runtime: security properties and grants; contacts bound to the live session; every email-change outcome, the attempt budget, expiry, delivery failure (audited), a concurrent claim, the refused start audited as denied, the new address on the account and the patient, the old one free, the Google link of the old address revoked and the explicit one kept, the open recovery code invalidated and the email check kept, the other device's session ended and the caller's family kept, a patient account that is also workforce refused at the start and at completion, a staff record's address unavailable, audit without addresses, no delete; phone changes in both Nigerian forms, phone sign-in following the change, the hourly limits, an unreadable stored number written again as a change and a readable one unchanged; readiness true after a sign-up patient's email change, a NIN-route patient's phone change and a migrated patient's added email where 0057's body answers false, and still false for an unrecorded write or a patient promoted after the rekey; profile details and photo commands, CHECKs and session binding; the patient's health information saved and read in a fresh patient-self context, stale versions, refusals, no direct write, a clinician reading it with a grant at its facility and purpose and not without, after the grant ends or at another facility; the clinician's ehr.record.read audit row a view in the patient's access log; each fix reverted alone fails it), and seven definer suites pass with the NOSUPERUSER owner. With 20,000 active enrollments the replaced readiness function runs in 160-200 ms (0057's 210-280 ms), 180-250 ms with 2,000 contact changes. Old images on this schema: the previous Identity and EHR call none of the new functions and read none of the new tables; sign-up and the NIN route get 0057's readiness answer while no contact change exists. Applied migrations 0001-0093 are unchanged.
